subject: RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
parts:
Greetings. I noticed that by using RStudio/knitr/pandoc one can create HTML
slides from R Markdown files. This seems very convenient, but I've had
problems with my first attempt at it.

I don't seem to be able to use traditional graphics to make slides. I've
tried a number of variations on this, but I think the following sums it up.

I took Yihui's example file, 009-slides.Rmd, and modified it to contain a
short section with a traditional plot command:

$ diff 009-slides.Rmd knitr-examples/009-slides.Rmd
32,38d31
< # What about traditional graphics?
< ```{r tradGraph, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
<
< plot(rnorm(100))
<
< ```
<

I converted the modified file using pandoc:

$ pandoc -s -S -i -t dzslides --mathjax 009-slides.md -o \
009-slides-converted.html

When I view 009-slides-converted.html, I see everything, including the figure
produced by "qplot" in the "Graphics too" section, EXCEPT that all I see on my
"What about traditional graphics?" slide is the R command:

plot(rnorm(100))

on an otherwise completely black background. Can somebody tell me what I'm
doing wrong?

Note that I've tried many variations of this with different figure sizes, etc.
Everything always displays fine in the HTML preview, for instance. Nothing
makes the final, converted-to-slides version any better.

All of the relevant software is pretty current. Please see the appended for
some details.

Thanks.

-- Mike

parts: You said that your plot is on a black background, so I think the plot really is there, you just cannot see it.  By default base graphics will plot black with a transparent background, so you have black on black.  Try changing your plotting colors, or specify a non-transparent background for the plot (possibly using par(bg='white') or you may need to set an option to the graphics device).  Or you could change the background of the slides so that the black shows up.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
parts:
Greg is correct. The plot is indeed there, and you cannot see it just
because its background is transparent; par(bg='white') will solve the
problem.

BTW, the default dzslides template from Pandoc does not seem to work
very well with images, and you may end up with modifying the template
(e.g. adjusting certain CSS rules).

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
parts:
Thanks, guys.  I'm embarrassed to admit that the black background was indeed the problem (this not being my first polka).

A few related remarks:

(1) I couldn't find a way to set the background globally -- I had to use par(bg=...) in each code block.

(2) I see that one could tweak the CSS, and that's sometimes fun and interesting, but I'd prefer not to have to do it routinely.

(3) I used "dzslides" just because that's what I saw in the little tutorials by Yihui and Gaston.  It turns out that, from my perspective at least, the whole thing works much better if I specify the type as "slidy".  Is there any reason not to do that?

Thanks again,

-- Mike

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?

1. you can define a chunk hook for that: http://yihui.name/knitr/hooks
see lines 43/47-49 for example:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/examples/knitr-manual.Rnw

3. I do not quite remember the reason. Perhaps it is because dzslides
is self-contained -- everything (JS and CSS) is embedded in a single
HTML file.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
parts:
Thanks, Yihui.  I see that the HTML file produced by pandoc/slidy does indeed use links to www.w3.org to define its styles and scripts.  I can see that this would be a drawback in some cases, although I suppose it would be easy enough to download the relevant styles and scripts and then edit the HTML file to refer to the local copies.

-- Mike

No need to manually edit the file; pandoc lets you point to local copies for offline projects (--self-contained i believe).
